ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, $O$ is the center of the semicircle, and $C$, $D$ are two points on the semicircle. Connect $CD$, $BD$, $AD$, where $CD=BD$. Extend $AC$ to intersect the extension of $BD$ at point $E$. Given that $CD=DE$; if $AC=6$ and the radius $OB=5$, find the length of $BD$.
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} In right triangle $\triangle ACB$, we have $BC=\sqrt{AB^{2}-AC^{2}}=\sqrt{10^{2}-6^{2}}=8$.\\
Since $CD=DE$ and $CD=BD$,\\
it follows that $BD=ED$.\\
In $\triangle ADB$ and $\triangle ADE$, we have\\
$\left\{\begin{array}{l}
AD=AD \\
\angle ADB=\angle EDA \\
BD=ED
\end{array}\right.$,\\
therefore, $\triangle ADB \cong \triangle ADE \text{ (SAS)}$,\\
thus, $AE=AB=10$,\\
hence, $CE=AE-AC=10-6=4$,\\
In right triangle $\triangle ECB$, $BE=\sqrt{CE^{2}+CB^{2}}=\sqrt{4^{2}+8^{2}}=4\sqrt{5}$,\\
therefore, $BD=\frac{1}{2}BE=2\sqrt{5}=\boxed{2\sqrt{5}}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The diagram shows a semicircle with horizontal diameter AB and center O on AB. Points C and D lie on the arc. Segment AC is extended past C to meet the extension of line BD at E, so A, C, E are collinear and B, D, E are collinear, with D between B and E. Segments AD, BD, CD are drawn. Reasoning: Since AB is the diameter and OB = 5, AB = 2OB = 10. Because C lies on the semicircle with diameter AB, angle ACB is a right angle. Given AC = 6, in right triangle ACB, BC = sqrt(AB^2 - AC^2) = sqrt(10^2 - 6^2) = sqrt(64) = 8. The conditions give CD = BD and CD = DE, hence BD = DE. Since B, D, E are collinear, D is the midpoint of BE. Also D lies on the semicircle with diameter AB, so angle ADB is right; because B, D, E are collinear, AD is perpendicular to BE. Thus AD is the perpendicular bisector of BE, so A is equidistant from B and E, giving AE = AB = 10. Therefore CE = AE - AC = 10 - 6 = 4. Since CE lies along AC and AC is perpendicular to CB, triangle ECB is right at C. Hence BE = sqrt(CE^2 + CB^2) = sqrt(4^2 + 8^2) = sqrt(80) = 4sqrt(5). Since D is the midpoint of BE, BD = BE/2 = 2sqrt(5).
